# `sesam ls` takes each secret's metadata from the config entry that declares
# it. Paths in a sub-config are relative to that file, so sub/x.txt and the
# root x.txt must not be mixed up.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin
exec sesam add x.txt
exec sesam add --nested sub/x.txt
exec sh -c 'printf "    desc: SUB-ONLY\n" >> sub/sesam.yml'

exec sesam ls --json
stdout '(?s)"revealed_path": "sub/x.txt",[^]]*\][^}]*"desc": "SUB-ONLY"'
! stdout '(?s)"revealed_path": "x.txt",[^]]*\][^}]*"desc"'

-- x.txt --
root
-- sub/x.txt --
sub
